title: Comms for DOJ Statement of Interest in OAI Case (Department of Justice, Executive Office for United States Attorneys)

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Communications that the Department of Justice sent to or received from OpenAI (OAI), OAI's lobbyists, or OAI's attorneys about the Statement of Interest of the United States filed in the S.D.N.Y. matter In re: OpenAI, Inc., 25-md-3143 (SHS) (OTW), including the preparation of the Statement of Interest. This statement was filed on September 1, 2026 by Michael Weisbuch, who is Senior Counsel to the Associate Attorney General.  It is Document 1682 on the docket,

Please the following email domains and email address as search terms in conducting the request to limit the scope to communication to or from OAI and its lobbyists and attorneys:
@openai.com
@mofo.com
@lw.com
openai@politicomlaw.com

DOJ can limit its custodians to the head of the office receiving this request and the head's immediate aides/deputies, Michael Weisbuch (Michael.Weisbuch@usdoj.gov), Associate AG Stanley E. Woodward, and Assistant Attorney General Brett Shumate.

The time frame of the search is June 1, 2026-September 2, 2026.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Department of Energy

title: Virginia Child Support System (vCHAMPS/APECS) Advance Planning Documents

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Virginia Child Support System (vCHAMPS/APECS) Advance Planning Documents
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

All Advance Planning Documents (APDs) submitted by the Virginia Department of Social Services, Division of Child Support Enforcement, to the Office of Child Support Services (OCSE, formerly OCSS) for Virginia's project to modernize or replace its child support system, APECS. The project was also known as vCHAMPS, the Child Support System Modernization (CSSM) Project, Child Support Enforcement Modernization, and the Child Support Refactoring Project.

Date range: January 1, 2020 to present.

This includes, but is not limited to:
1. Planning APD (PAPD)
2. Streamlined Feasibility Study, including its cost-benefit analysis
3. Implementation APD (IAPD)
4. Each Annual APD Update
5. Each As-Needed APD Update
6. OCSS approval, conditional approval, or disapproval letters for each

These records are likely held by OCSE, which reviews state child support system APDs.

I agree to pay up to $100 in fees without further approval. Please contact me only if fees will exceed that amount.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Yax Falk

title: CCSO Policies and Procedures on Releases

communications.subject: Illinois Freedom of Information Act. Request: CCSO Policies and Procedures on Releases
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

Policies and process documents relating to release of an individual in custody once a judge has decided that they are to be released:
- Steps and timeline to release a individual in custody after a judge has decided they should be released
- Rules or guidelines on maximum wait times to be released
- Resources that people entitled to while waiting to be release
E.g. food, water, access to a phone, bathroom
- Resources that a released individual is entitled to receive once they are free to go
E.g. personal property, bus passes, warm clothing in winter, information and resources
if they can make a call, how many, how long it can last

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

4

title: Multnomah County Medical Examiner's Office: Public records request: disposition records, unidentified female decedent, Portland, October 18, 1994

communications.subject: Oregon Public Records Law Request: Multnomah County Medical Examiner's Office: Public records request: disposition records, unidentified female decedent, Portland, October 18, 1994
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Oregon Public Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

I request copies of the following records concerning an unidentified adult female found deceased in a Portland hotel room on October 18, 1994. This unidentified adult female is listed as NamUs #UP9936, has a Portland Police Bureau agency case number of 94-99422, and has an Oregon State Police Medical Examiner's Office agency case number of 94-2962. The decedent is unidentified and was recorded under an
alias at hotel check-in.

The NAMUS listing can be found online at:
https://www.namus.gov/UnidentifiedPersons/Case#/9936/contacts?nav

There is a Websleuth's thread located online at:
https://websleuths.com/threads/or-portland-whtfem-35-55-up9936-suicide-hotel-surgical-scars-lft-knee-rt-breast-dec94.165575/

Under the Oregon Public Records Law (ORS 192.311 et seq.), I request copies of the following records concerning an unidentified adult female found deceased in a Portland hotel room on October 18, 1994:

1. Any order for disposition of the body (burial, cremation, or reduction) issued by a medical examiner or sheriff, and any burial, cremation, or reduction permit.

2. The verified statement of expenses and any related report of death filed with the Board of County Commissioners (ORS 146.121).

3. Records identifying the funeral home, contractor, or cemetery used, and the date and location of disposition, including any plot, grave, niche, or common-grave record.

4. Any invoice, payment record, or contract for the disposition.

5. Any record of biological samples, tissue, hair, bone, slides, or dental records retained from the autopsy, and their current location.

6. If any responsive record has been destroyed, the applicable retention schedule and any destruction certificate.

I ask that fees be waived or reduced because this is in the public interest. I am an independent researcher and I have a theory as to the identity of this unidentified person. 

Thank you for the work that the Multnomah County Medical Examiner's Office does each and every day.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

Robert Delaware
